rule: NEVER let a safety or authorization gate arrive at its permissive branch by fall-through; compute the blocking verdict as the default and require affirmative, validated evidence to override it, so that malformed, missing, or unevaluable state lands in the blocking branch.
why: A protective check that fails open is weakest against exactly the corrupted inputs it exists to defend against.
sourceFailure: kstack-jira.mjs preMutationDuplicateGate: Date.parse(entry.at) on a malformed/missing timestamp produces NaN; NaN < VERIFY_CLEAR_MIN_AGE_MS evaluates false, so control fell through to the verify-clear (safe-to-POST) branch instead of blocking. Undetected by tests because the age comparison used raw Date.now() instead of the injectable clock used everywhere else in the codebase.

rule: NEVER let a bulk or blanket "dismiss all" resolution path operate across evidence of mixed provenance. Partition candidates by origin and permit blanket dismissal only for externally-derived, inferential matches, requiring evidence the system recorded about its own side-effecting actions to be resolved individually by naming the specific artifact it produced.
why: A blanket clear that reaches self-recorded evidence silently disarms every downstream gate that depends on that evidence.
sourceFailure: kstack-jira.mjs resolveDraft: the --distinct branch's guard only blocks bulk dismissal from 'unknown' state when there is NO direct evidence; when direct evidence of the queue's own successful POST exists, --distinct dismisses it along with search-derived candidates via queueAudit('duplicate-dismissed', { dismissedKeys: candidates }), silently reopening the double-POST control that submit's pre-send duplicate gate (SEC-R17-3) was built to close.

rule: NEVER add a new event type or a new exit path to a flow whose invariants live in enumerated recognizers or per-path conventions without, in the same change, updating every encoding of that contract -- each list that must now recognize the new case, and each obligation the new path must itself perform -- or collapsing them into one shared helper that no path can bypass.
why: A contract duplicated across sites fails silently at exactly the site never told about the new case.
sourceFailure: kstack-jira.mjs: (a) reconcileDraft's aborted-before-post recovery writes a new submit-recovered audit event, but unresolvedSearchEvidence()'s enumerated resolving-event set (verify-clear/verify-confirmed/duplicate-acknowledged/duplicate-dismissed) was never updated to recognize it, forcing an unnecessary extra verification poll on a case the spec says should need none; (b) releaseDraftLock's 'release claim displaced another holder and was restored' exit path fails with EXIT.LOCK_FENCED_DIRTY like its three sibling paths, but unlike them does not call writeOrphan() first, losing the residue sidecar the fenced-exit contract depends on.

rule: NEVER let a shared setup path -- config load, bootstrap, DI construction -- open, read, or parse a resource that only some callers consume; validate and materialize a credential, file, handle, or connection inside the command that actually uses it, at the moment it uses it.
why: A precondition placed in the shared path silently becomes a precondition of every caller, including the one deliberately designed to have none.
sourceFailure: kstack-config.mjs's validateCredentialFileConfig opens, reads, and JSON.parses the credential file at config-load time inside loadJiraState(), which every Jira command calls including the fully-offline draft command that the design's SS5/SS9 explicitly require to work with no credential available (so it can be reached from a sandboxed/credential-free calling context). This silently coupled an operation with zero preconditions to a resource it never touches, making draft fail closed whenever the credential file is absent, unreadable, or malformed.

rule: NEVER classify a state whose defining measurement is missing or unparseable under an exit code that promises callers a transient, bounded wait — because a parse-failure sentinel such as age 0 satisfies the "young enough to retry" predicate forever, so callers loop indefinitely against a condition only human repair can clear.
why: an unmeasurable-age sentinel of 0 always compares as younger than any floor, making a supposedly transient exit code permanently, silently unresolvable
sourceFailure: kstack-jira.mjs's EXIT.INDEX_LAG_BLOCKED remediation routed markers with an unparseable/missing timestamp to the new transient-wait exit code because youngestMarkerAgeMs() returns 0 (not Infinity/error) on unparseable Date.parse, and the round-1 diff flipped the pre-existing 'missing timestamp' test's expected exit code to match the new (wrong) behavior instead of catching the regression

rule: NEVER treat a same-UID local credential-disposition attestation as a Q3 security boundary; the subject can forge the claim.
why: The attesting actor cannot independently verify credential absence or revocation against itself.
sourceFailure: Round 11 replaced verification with a self-produced credential-disposition assertion and combined confidence fell from 62 to 41.

rule: NEVER replace bounded reviewed RegExp matchers with a bespoke NFA without a demonstrated security requirement; the custom engine adds attack surface and correctness risk.
why: The existing capped and gated RegExp set is the smaller reviewed security mechanism.
sourceFailure: Rounds 12 and 13 introduced a custom NFA compiler and interpreter while combined confidence fell from 41 to 38 and then 30.

rule: NEVER require a private Git snapshot solely to hide reconstructable historical helper bytes from a same-UID actor; reconstruction adds no capability beyond the threat model.
why: Credential validity is a separate owner residual-risk fact rather than a capability created by byte recovery.
sourceFailure: The round-10 history blocker became snapshot architecture by round 13, but the same-UID actor already had arbitrary code execution and confidence reached 30 before falling to 18.

rule: ALWAYS prefer a pinned static environment-scrubber command over per-platform native launchers for the v1 hook vehicle; it minimizes signing and supply-chain surface.
why: Native launchers add toolchain, provenance, signing, notarization, distribution, and incident-response obligations.
sourceFailure: Rounds 13 and 14 considered native launchers while combined confidence fell from 38 to 30 and then 18, and the simpler static scrubber met the v1 need.

rule: NEVER scope a static-graph/capability-analysis claim to the entire distributed artifact including unrelated third-party dependencies; scope it to the actual safety-relevant module boundary.
why: because unrelated dependency capabilities do not establish reachability on the credential/tool-call path
sourceFailure: round-12-redo's closed-artifact-universe framework created a self-contradictory preview-cap timing requirement and an unbounded capability-analysis obligation over pglite/node-gyp, dropping confidence from 74 to 66

rule: NEVER call a bounded safety-module graph complete until its roots, non-ESM launch manifest, retained-process argv and environment, constructor seams, wire grammar, and upgrade selection order are exact and testable.
why: because an omitted edge can bypass an otherwise correct narrow import graph
sourceFailure: round-12-redo2 narrowed analysis correctly but left hooks launch, Git spawn hardening, constructor injection, response schemas, and pre-refresh upgrade selection incomplete, dropping confidence from 74 to 64

rule: NEVER call a bounded capability-free artifact exact while its launcher has a CWD/environment fallback, its Git child honors local config/helper execution, or its first-party check is semantic rather than a finite named lint.
why: Those residual paths can execute or open content outside the enumerated roots even when roots, argv, schemas, and file names are otherwise explicit.
sourceFailure: round-12-redo3 applied ten localized fixes but retained a dot launch fallback, local Git config/helper paths, an undefined content digest, and a semantic protected-path analysis; combined confidence fell from 74 to 43
